title: How to Set School Fees in Kenya: Fee Structure Guide (2026)
h1: How to Set School Fees in Kenya: A Fee Structure Guide (2026)
description: How to set school fees in Kenya — costing your real per-term expenses, building a clear fee structure, communicating it to parents, and avoiding disputes.
primaryKeyword: how to set school fees in Kenya
author: SQUL Team
intro: A fee structure is a promise: this is what the school needs, and this is what each learner pays for. Get it wrong and you either run short by mid-term or spend the term defending the numbers to angry parents. This guide shows **how to set school fees in Kenya** from real costs, not guesswork. It is part of our guide to [how to manage a school in Kenya](/blog/how-to-manage-a-school-in-kenya).
We will cover costing, the components of a structure, how to present it, and how to review it each year without surprises.

items: **Lump sums hide everything.** "KES 40,000 per term" tells a parent nothing about what they are buying.
**Costs move.** Food, fuel and utilities rise between terms; a structure that never changes runs short.
**Two currencies of expectation.** Parents compare with neighbours; the school must cost its own reality.
**No single source.** If the fee structure lives in a spreadsheet only the bursar understands, disputes multiply.

blocks.text: A fee structure is the output of a budget, not a guess. Take your term costs and divide them across the learners who will actually attend.

items.title: Total your term costs
items.text: Staff, boarding (food, utilities, matron), learning materials, facilities and maintenance, transport, activities, administration, and a contingency.

items.title: Divide by planned enrolment
items.text: Cost per learner = total costs ÷ expected learners. Use conservative enrolment.

items.title: Separate boarding from day
items.text: Boarders carry food and utilities the day section does not. Cost each separately.

items.title: Set the structure
items.text: Turn the per-learner cost into clear line items parents can see.

blocks.title: Budget on conservative enrolment
blocks.text: If you set fees on an optimistic headcount and enrolment misses, every learner is undercharged. Cost for the number you can defend.

sections.heading: What a good fee structure contains

blocks.caption: A transparent structure beats a single number.

blocks.text: Breaking it out makes the total defensible: a parent can see why a boarder pays more, and the school can adjust one line without disturbing the rest.

items: **Send it early** — before the term ends, so families can plan. Late structures invite resistance.
**Explain, don't just announce** — one line per component does the work.
**Give the payment channel clearly** — Paybill or till, and the account reference (ideally the learner's admission number).
**Confirm every payment** — a receipt on WhatsApp or SMS ends the "did you receive it?" questions.

blocks.text: Communicating fees and confirming payments are the same job. See [fee reminders over SMS and WhatsApp](/blog/school-fee-reminder-sms-whatsapp-kenya).

Review once a year, calmly, against last year's actuals — not in a panic mid-term. Ask: did any cost line rise faster than planned? Did enrolment hold? Did arrears grow? A small, explained annual adjustment is far easier for parents than a large emergency one.

blocks.title: Tie fees to collection
blocks.text: A perfect structure that you cannot collect still fails. Pair it with automated reconciliation and reminders — see [how to reduce fee arrears](/blog/how-to-reduce-school-fee-arrears-kenya).

items: **Copying neighbouring schools** instead of costing your own.
**One lump sum** with no explanation of what it covers.
**No contingency** for repairs and price rises.
**Announcing late**, leaving families no time to plan.
**Ignoring arrears** when setting next year's fees.

faqs.question: How are school fees calculated in Kenya?
faqs.answer: Total your term costs (staff, boarding, learning, facilities, transport, activities, admin, contingency), divide by conservative planned enrolment, and separate boarding from day learners. That per-learner figure becomes your fee structure.

faqs.question: Should a school charge one fee or break it down?
faqs.answer: Break it down. A transparent structure — tuition, boarding, activities, development — is more defensible and lets the school adjust one component without renegotiating the whole fee.

faqs.question: When should parents be told about fees?
faqs.answer: Before the term ends, with the structure and payment details, so families can plan. Late announcements cause avoidable disputes.

faqs.question: How do we handle fee arrears?
faqs.answer: Keep a live arrears view by class, confirm every payment immediately, and send staged reminders over WhatsApp and SMS. Automated reconciliation means reminders reach only real defaulters.

faqs.question: Can fees change mid-year?
faqs.answer: Review annually against actuals. Mid-term changes are hard to justify and damage trust; plan for cost rises in the annual review instead.
